title: Transmembrane pressure control strategies for minimising irreversible fouling in continuous whey protein ultrafiltration

record.title: Transmembrane pressure control strategies for minimising irreversible fouling in continuous whey protein ultrafiltration
record.abstract: A pilot-scale cross-flow ultrafiltration system (10 m² polyethersulphone, 10 kDa) was used to investigate three transmembrane pressure (TMP) control strategies during continuous concentration of sweet whey protein from an initial 0.9% total protein to a target 4.5% total protein. Strategy 1 maintained constant TMP at 2.5 bar; Strategy 2 applied a stepwise TMP ramp from 1.0 to 3.5 bar over 120 min; Strategy 3 implemented feedback TMP reduction triggered when the flux decline rate exceeded 5% per 10 min. After 8-hour runs, irreversible fouling resistance was 31% lower under Strategy 3 compared with Strategy 1, and total volumetric throughput was equivalent within 4%. Protein transmission at the permeate side was maintained below 2% in all runs. Energy consumption per kilogram of processed protein was reduced by 12% under Strategy 3. The findings support closed-loop TMP management as a practical approach to extending membrane service intervals.
